name: Editorial fashion
means: The garment is the subject and the person is the armature: one decisive light raking across fabric, a held stylised pose, a clean or deliberately stark setting, and empty frame left where the magazine's type would go.
prose: an editorial fashion photograph, a single hard studio light raking across the garment to reveal its fabric and cut, the model in a held stylised pose, clean seamless backdrop, medium format sharpness across the garment, generous empty space in the upper frame, restrained colour palette
negative_add: snapshot, casual, cluttered background, soft flattering light, illustration, anime
works_for: video moderately. Held poses and a plain backdrop are friendly to i2v; fabric is not, and drape and weave crawl between frames. Inferred.
note: This card is mostly a GARMENT problem, and that is where it fails. 'Editorial', 'high fashion' and 'stylish' are quality words, and this box renders nouns - the project already learned that the hard way, which is why the character cards keep clothing in explicit wear tags rather than trusting an adjective. Name the garment: a black wool double-breasted coat with exaggerated shoulders, a floor-length pleated silk skirt. Then name the light. Keep the negative space in the prompt for a second reason too - qwen renders literal quoted text well, so if you actually want a cover line, that is where it goes. Unavailable on the anime checkpoint in this idiom. | Downgraded to untested: NOTHING in this library was rendered when it was authored, so every strength and engine call is a considered prediction. This project's own standard - written on the Illustrious checkpoint card - is that a recommendation is not a measurement.
verdict: Slightly more posed and styled than the control, but the difference is small enough to be seed noise. Use studio_portrait unless you specifically need the styling.
verified_by: Looked at, against the no-style control at the same seed with the same subject. studio/_tools/style_examples.py
